correctness.rationale: The transient generator is explicitly derived from the occupancy transitions. The rational survival resolvent and its P=ab derivative at fixed S=a+b are checked symbolically. The negative derivative factors into Laplace transforms of two strictly positive kernels: a nonnegative addition to survival and the normalized B-to-singleton transition probabilities. Their convolution is strictly positive at every t>0. The c=0 case follows from the three-exponential convolution identity; the proof covers all positive a,b and all finite c>=0, including balanced rates by one-sided differentiation. Exact rational mean examples and 216 finite-time semigroup computations corroborate, but do not substitute for, the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected ecological literature motivates protecting heterogeneous patches primarily via expected lifetime or qualitative landscape rankings, rather than an exact all-horizon strict stochastic comparison at a fixed total extinction rate. The most relevant fully accessible stochastic-order paper, Corujo–Valdés–Laria (arXiv:1804.03098), treats cold/warm standby systems with principal-versus-spare slots and two transient operational states. Its propositions do not cover the current three-transient-state two-patch process nor fixed-sum hazard redistribution. The c=0 independent-parallel special case is classical and explicitly not asserted as novel. Full text of Etienne–Heesterbeek (2001) was inaccessible, so equivalent prior art remains a recorded substantive uncertainty.
residual_risks: Full text of Etienne–Heesterbeek (2001), an especially pertinent extinction-rate management study, could not be inspected; an identical or stronger but unreported theorem might occur in its proofs or appendices.
Full text of Frank (2005) was inaccessible; only its publisher abstract and chronology were directly available.
Other older repairable active-parallel models may have unindexed equivalent stochastic-majorization statements; search coverage is not uniqueness proof.
No independent mathematical review has been performed.

value.rationale: A natural conservation intervention constraint fixes the sum of local extinction hazards while redistributing them between two habitat patches. The finding supplies a strict usual-stochastic-order theorem at every time horizon with recolonization, which is stronger than mean-lifetime allocation rules and is not implied by static no-recolonization reliability. The exact structural positivity argument settles the general finite-rate two-patch classification under the stated symmetry, rather than computing an arbitrary small case. The ecological interpretation is limited to the specified Markov occupancy model.
